claims.claim: Intersect requests 1,193,000 ADA, stated as $298,250, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3.
Execution of the work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.
The proposal says all expenditure will be fully accounted for and any unspent funds returned to the Cardano treasury.
The proposal states that WP3 independent technical reviews will use formal conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal claims the TSC support is foundational technical governance capacity needed for Cardano to function effectively as a decentralized ecosystem.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting results and audit materials.
The proposal states the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit at submission and links to the relevant governance action.
The proposal says independent audits and assurance will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverables, controls, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

Intersect states it will use Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multisig-like administrative permissions, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for tracking funds.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of Intersect Technical Steering Committee support, with budgeted work packages, governance-process references, smart-contract fund administration details, and assertions of accounting, audits, oversight, and treasury return of unspent funds.
